summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (Jan 2.23/4036)

summary: New sense 1a: (mit ʕal-) nach etwas suchen
rationale: ʕal- introduces the thing sought, contrasting with b- for the place searched and with directly searched containers. Single attestation.

rationale: The supplied corpus verse reads “bi waṣṭa di ḥukume d mfatšət as sanduqayḏe”. The entry adds an i between d and the verb mfatšət. This is an extra vowel/syllable, rather than a change in clitic boundaries.

summary: b- marks the searched place or container (house, pockets, loads); direct nominal objects name searched interiors or boxes, and suffixes index searched people. The new ʕal-construction instead names what the searcher hopes to find.
Tactile exploration is already represented at LB 154 and confirmed by Talay 1/154. The blind giant at PrS 10/22 adds a clearer human-context example without another tactile sense.
The same prospective MAC instruction has gabayxu and a left-dislocated cellar resumed by -la. These alternate search-domain encodings without an additional numbered sense.
Infectum g-/unprefixed forms occur in prospective search scenarios. German begannen at Talay 1/39 does not establish a different box or an inchoative lexical sense.
The only inherited Infectum-wa item mixes Turoyo, English and Russian metaglosses and lacks a citation/translation. It is retained as an editorial problem rather than silently completed.
taftiš at 68/54 is a borrowed inspection event noun. Its nominal boundary remains unresolved; it is not published as a new Infinitiv box.
Jan English is machine translation [MT]. II.1 assignments follow the actual searched domains and clauses in the Turoyo.

The original plus round-1 Preterit and Infectum cells have five examples each. Border inspection, baggage inspection and human searches confirm the inherited range rather than fill a remaining routine gap.

Jan 2.10/2295 juxtaposes kəmfatəš and bare d mfatəš, with the latter purpose-directed and a suitcase patient. Jan 2.10/2296 has a fronted human patient ruḥani. None establishes a different search sense.

The Infinitiv fətošo is supported by nominal preposition mu- and parallel ḥzoyo/qroyo. It adds a native-shaped nominal box without resolving whether the round-1 taftiš is a separate borrowed event noun.
Written discussion of information and the Scripture passage extend the search domain. The action remains search/examination and is not promoted to a new technical sense.
The unresolved original Infectum-wa checkpoint quotation and round-1 ʕal-target subsense 1a are retained; no Jan evidence here repairs the incomplete quotation or directly adds a ʕal-target example.
